raw_text:
VERDICT goal: the delta's own goal is to close the prior review's confirmed staleness gap — the context-manifest cache stamped the paths the built manifest named but omitted agent_root/config.toml, which _read_agent_config reads and which drives budget.limit_bytes, the budget source and the fallback instruction filenames — and to make the shared verdict-input stamp see an in-place edit of a run file rather than only an add or remove. The fix records every path the build consults as it reads them into manifest['input_paths'] (the agent config unconditionally, the scanned directories, the project chain, the skill roots and the discovered SKILL.md files) and derives the stamp from that record via _manifest_file_paths, so stamp and computation share one source; the verdict stamp now names each run file by name beside the run-directory stamp; PICK_INPUT_CACHE_VERSION is bumped 1 to 2 to retire entries written under the earlier stamp shape. The bounded-pick goal of the parent node is unchanged by this delta.
VERDICT done_when: the delta's measures are met and I reproduced them independently in a scratch tree extracted at e8745033048cb67247b6f6cc2bbc4f3ed8b01dac: the new-file arm is 7 passed, EXIT=0, and the full head arm is 108 passed, EXIT=0; the added real-fixture equivalence test test_cached_context_manifest_tracks_every_input_it_reads builds the real context manifest on a fixture repository and moves each input in turn, config.toml included, asserting cached equals uncached; my own negative control removes the config.toml line from input_paths and reds that test at the config.toml change alone (1 failed, EXIT=1), so the test discriminates.
VERDICT write_paths: the reviewed delta is a single commit, e8745033048cb67247b6f6cc2bbc4f3ed8b01dac, touching exactly five paths, every one inside the run's declared grant (reckon/agent_context.py, reckon/capabilities.py, reckon/crew/routing.py, tests/test_picker_fresh_process_pick.py, docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-fresh-process-pick.html); the plan, project index and peer paths are untouched and the reviewed worktree is clean at head.
VERDICT manifest: read against the tree; status complete, commits oldest-first a63d72b8e, 21f99fdee, e87450330, after_suite 0 failed at e87450330 (108 passed), baseline_suite 0 failed at bd39abcff (101 passed), negative control (negative_control2.log) 1 failed at 21f99fde under the restored pre-fix stamp.
VERDICT diff: read e8745033048cb67247b6f6cc2bbc4f3ed8b01dac against 21f99fdee85a0b4c301d8297b151655b8ebecdc7; the delta adds input_paths to build_context_manifest, makes _manifest_file_paths read input_paths first, and returns the scanned directories from _project_instruction_chain; it adds a per-run-file list to _verdict_input_stamp; it bumps the cache version; it rewrites the fragment's equivalence paragraph and gate line to the delivered head; and it adds the real-fixture context test.
VERDICT call_sites: verified 2 production call site(s)

SCORE goal_fidelity: 18
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: the confirmed config.toml staleness gap is closed and verified — config.toml is now stamped unconditionally and my independent mutation reopens the failure — and the fragment's stale intermediate arm (106 passed at a63d72b8e) is corrected to the delivered head (108 passed, EXIT=0); deducted because the fragment's phase table still lists pre-pick reads (ledger rows, budget snapshot, template render) in a table framed for the bounded call, a framing carried from the prior review and untouched by this commit, and because the 'cannot drift' comment overstates the guarantee: input_paths is assembled from the values the build returned, so a future read whose result is not threaded into input_paths would stamp nothing.
SCORE evidence: 17
JUSTIFICATION evidence: independently reproduced in a scratch tree at e8745033048cb67247b6f6cc2bbc4f3ed8b01dac (new-file 7 passed EXIT=0; full head 108 passed EXIT=0) and I reproduced a discriminating negative control (remove config.toml from input_paths -> the added test fails at the config.toml change, EXIT=1), and the new equivalence test now uses the real build_context_manifest on a fixture repository rather than stubs, closing the prior review's synthetic-fixture deduction for the context manifest; deducted because the verdict-input stamp extension ships with no test of its own (the in-place run-file edit it claims to catch is untested), and because the base arm's log base.log carries no EXIT line, so its exit status rests on the pass summary rather than a recorded code.
SCORE scope_discipline: 19
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: one commit, five paths, all inside the run's declared grant; ruff with the repo's own config reports 12 findings at base over the four source/test files and 12 at head, so the commit adds none; the plan, project index and peer paths are untouched and the fragment is an in-grant evidence path.
SCORE durability: 17
JUSTIFICATION durability: the PICK_INPUT_CACHE_VERSION 1->2 bump is required and correct — without it a v1 entry would re-stamp under the new reader from a value lacking input_paths and could serve stale — and the stamp is derived from the built value so it tracks the computation; I confirmed the verdict stamp's glob (*.json under runs/) matches ledger._run_files, which load() iterates, so add, remove and in-place edit all move it; the negative control reproduces; deducted because the verdict-input stamp change is untested and because the can't-drift property depends on future authors continuing to thread new reads through input_paths.
SCORE fit: 18
JUSTIFICATION fit: the fix reuses the existing cached_pick_input_stamped idiom and threads the consulted paths through the manifest itself, so the record the stamp reads is the same artifact a reader can inspect; the diff is minimal and the fragment update is confined to the two lines the change made stale; deducted because the run-directory stamp is retained redundantly beside the new per-run list, and the 'cannot drift' docstring claims more than the construction guarantees.
FINDING follow-on tests/test_picker_fresh_process_pick.py the per-run-file verdict stamp added to routing._verdict_input_stamp ships without a test; the same shape the context test covers — edit a run file in place and assert the cached shared verdict inputs recompute — would pin it, since the change's whole point is that a directory mtime does not move on an in-place edit.
FINDING follow-on reckon/agent_context.py the 'so the stamp and the computation cannot drift' comment overstates the construction: input_paths collects the paths the build's return values name, so a new read whose result is not routed into an in-grant input_paths entry (a new manifest field) would be stamped by nothing; naming the invariant 'derived from the paths the returned manifest names' would be accurate.
